_comment: n8n fabric process workflows (AGENTS.md §23.23 10.0.0 ACTIVE: n8n owns FLOW, the host owns authority and evidence). One entry per business process the fabric owns or is about to own. The generator (scripts/n8n_workflow_templates.py build-fabric) reads this file plus the process's PipelineManifest@v1 (step order, stage schedules) and config/n8n_run_allowlist.json (per-step timeout) and renders one inactive workflow per process into docs/implementation/n8n-maturity/workflows/fabric/. Every runnable step calls the published Run Lane sub-workflow; a BLOCKED step never calls it and is recorded as status 'blocked' with its reason. depends_on names steps of the SAME stage that come EARLIER in the manifest (the shell runner's order stays a valid topological order, so shadow parity is comparable). mode is what the workflow requests: 'dry_run' until the cutover PR changes it (the executor's stage clamp also forces dry_run while a lane is at stage shadow). The step lanes, their allowlist entries, health contracts and effect keys are reviewed in the same PR as this file (packet docs/ops/packets/n8n-hermes-learning-flow-20261015/).

tag_engine.blocked: NO SAFE DRY RUN: without --apply, scripts/hermes_tag_engine.py retag() still calls lib.governed_cloud_generation.generate_cloud (process_id hermes_tag_engine) for up to llm_batch rows (_llm_tags), so a dry run spends a model call. Needs a --dry-run that skips _llm_tags plus an llm_route declaration (AGENTS.md §23.18 llm class) in its own code PR.

outcome_feedback_agent.blocked: SENDER (never-list, AGENTS.md §23.14): --apply calls lib/hermes_outcome_bus/alert_notifications.dispatch_alert_notifications -> _send_telegram -> telegram_alert.send_telegram. Its dry run is write-free, but a sender is never on the run allowlist; the send must become a host comms intent (§24.1) in a code PR first.

score_history_retention.blocked: DESTRUCTIVE RETENTION (never-list): --apply runs DELETE FROM hermes_score_history (scripts/hermes_score_history_retention.py). The allowlist never-list names destructive retention stages under any class; moving retention into n8n at all is an operator decision. Ordered after outcome_grader because the grader freezes score components before retention can delete them.

autonomous_self_tune.blocked: DESTRUCTIVE RETENTION (never-list): --apply runs self_purge (archived DELETEs through lib.retention_archive.managed_purge on hermes_embedding_queue, hermes_score_history, hermes_research_intelligence, hermes_external_research and the dead legacy tables, plus queue UPDATEs) together with the auto-graft. Split --learn (auto-graft, a learn-class writer) from --purge in a code PR before the learn half can be a lane; the purge half stays a host step.
